summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee advanced plans for 2027 anniversary events, including drone shows, history talks, parades, and fundraisers.
summary.summary: The Tricentennial Committee reviewed progress across dozens of planned community events celebrating Southborough's 300th anniversary in 2027. Library Director Ryan Donovan shared plans for funded historical lectures, while members discussed an AI-generated musical history concept, utility pole banners, and upcoming promotional efforts at Summer Nights. Key subcommittees also reported on cemetery reenactments, parade participant guidelines, a union-sponsored town bonfire, and ongoing commemorative brick and merchandise sales.

topics.title: Library historical lectures and event collaborations
topics.summary: Library Director Ryan Donovan presented ideas for town history programs co-hosted by the Southborough Library and the Senior Center. The Friends of the Library agreed to fully fund a tailored $750 local history lecture by the Gravestone Girls planned for spring. The committee and library are also exploring reviving the historic Strawberry Social, displaying reservoir photography exhibits, and coordinating dates for the History in Bloom event from April 15 to 17.
key_details: Friends of the Library agreed to fund the $750 fee for a tailored Southborough presentation by Gravestone Girls.
Gravestone rubbings were clarified to be illegal in Massachusetts, so the event will focus strictly on lectures.
Reviving the Strawberry Social would require advance ticketing and extra volunteer support due to high food-prep overhead.
History in Bloom dates were tentatively set for April 15-17.
A photography exhibit on the Quabbin and Sudbury reservoirs is being planned with the Friends of Quabbin.
topics.outcome: The committee and library will continue coordinating lecture schedules and exploring ticketed social events.

topics.title: AI-generated musical history concept presentation
topics.summary: A resident working with an artificial intelligence startup presented a 20-chapter, 70-minute AI-generated musical project chronicling Southborough's history. The committee discussed using individual snippets as promotional teasers on social media, background audio for presentations, or as a student project for local high schoolers. Members emphasized that any public materials must include disclaimers and undergo historical fact-checking.
key_details: The project consists of 20 short chapters covering topics including the Burnett family, Fay School, and the naming of Cordaville.
Committee members suggested extracting short clips rather than playing the full 70-minute recording at single events.
The presenter offered to supply a printed book version and summary notes for fact-checking.
Members noted AI historical narratives can contain inaccuracies and must be reviewed before promotional use.
topics.outcome: The presenter will share transcripts and written summaries with the committee for review.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the minutes from its June 10 meeting with a minor correction, with one member abstaining due to absence. The meeting concluded at 1:34:15 with an adjournment vote.
key_details: Minutes of June 10 were approved with one correction on line 37.
Andrew Dennington abstained from the minutes vote.
The next committee meeting was scheduled for August 12.
topics.outcome: Minutes were approved, and the meeting adjourned.

topics.title: Tricentennial utility pole banner project
topics.summary: The committee reviewed efforts to secure approval from National Grid and Verizon to hang commemorative banners across town. A total of 85 utility poles have been selected, primarily clustered along Central Street, Boston Road, and Main Street. Utility companies require individual photos and pole numbers for each location, and the committee is recruiting volunteers to photograph the poles.
key_details: 85 utility poles have been identified for commemorative banners.
Poles are clustered on Central Street, Boston Road toward Neary School, and Main Street.
National Grid and Verizon require photograph submissions with visible pole numbers for approval.
Members are seeking adult or student volunteers to photograph all 85 poles.
topics.outcome: Members will coordinate volunteer photographers to complete the photo submission packet.

topics.title: Event updates and promotion at Summer Nights
topics.summary: Members discussed placing the proposed Awareness Days on hold to focus resources on higher-priority events. The committee planned outreach for the town's Summer Nights celebration on August 22 to build awareness for the 2027 anniversary. Promotional strategies include distributing informational cards, promoting the newsletter, and coordinating announcements with the Recreation Department.
key_details: Awareness Days were moved to the back burner to avoid overtaxing committee members.
Promotion for 2027 signature events will begin at Summer Nights on August 22.
Promotional cards will direct residents to sign up for the Tricentennial newsletter.
Outreach materials will also be made available at Fall Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Committee members will prepare promotional materials for Summer Nights.

topics.title: Voices from the Grave and Historic House Tour planning
topics.summary: Subcommittee leaders reported on the Voices from the Grave cemetery reenactment planned for November. The working group has researched historical figures using university archives and is actively recruiting volunteer actors, especially men. Separately, the Historic House Tour group is working to finalize a lineup of approximately 12 historic properties and will give a formal report in September.
key_details: Voices from the Grave plans to feature about eight historical characters across two cemetery locations.
Research includes reviewing Rev. Nathan Stone's historical sermons archived at the University of Delaware.
Organizers are seeking local actors for approximately two hours of performances.
The Historic House Tour working group is targeting around 12 historic Southborough homes.
topics.outcome: Voices from the Grave organizers will recruit actors, and the House Tour group will present a full update in September.

topics.title: Parade, Drone Show, and Antique Firemen's Muster
topics.summary: The parade working group prepared draft participant contracts and a three-page standard of rules to distribute to prospective marching groups. Andrew Dennington confirmed the drone vendor has reserved January 1 and 2, 2027 on its schedule for the First Night and First Day events. Organizers of the Firemen's Muster requested officially renaming the event the Antique Firemen's Muster and discussed coordinating food truck permits with the Board of Health.
key_details: Parade working group developed a formal contract and three pages of operating rules for participants.
Oxen owners indicated they cannot commit until early 2027 due to livestock uncertainties.
The drone company confirmed Southborough is on its calendar for January 1 and 2, 2027.
The muster will officially be called the Antique Firemen's Muster.
Food trucks will need health certificates through Board of Health Director Taylor West, and portable restrooms are budgeted.
topics.outcome: Contracts will be issued to prospective parade participants, and muster organizers will coordinate food truck logistics.

topics.title: Hayrides, town bonfire, and time capsule
topics.summary: The chair reported that a historic mule-drawn hay wagon owned by the late Bob Seeley remains stored intact in a Southborough barn and could potentially be used for Heritage Day. The Southborough Firefighters Union agreed to organize and supervise the community bonfire, with timing to be coordinated alongside either Glo-SoBo or the winter drone show. Scout troops confirmed initial interest in participating in the time capsule project.
key_details: A historic hay wagon stored in Southborough is being evaluated for potential use as a Heritage Day shuttle.
The Southborough Firefighters Union agreed to take full operational responsibility for the town bonfire.
Bonfire timing options include pairing it with the winter drone show or the Glo-SoBo event.
Boy Scout and Girl Scout troops were contacted regarding the time capsule, with formal commitments expected by September.
topics.outcome: Discussions will continue with the Firefighters Union on bonfire scheduling and with scout troops on capsule contributions.

topics.title: Ceremonial Incorporation Day, brick sales, and merchandise
topics.summary: Members favored holding Ceremonial Incorporation Day at Heritage Park rather than the Town Common due to the flatter terrain, pending Select Board approval. Claire Reynolds joined the fundraising team to manage the commemorative brick order database. Merchandise sales have been strong, with large and extra-large t-shirts selling out, prompting an order of 78 additional shirts and discussions of an online store.
key_details: Heritage Park is the preferred site for Ceremonial Incorporation Day and time capsule burial, subject to Select Board approval.
Claire Reynolds was recruited to oversee commemorative brick orders and manufacturer entry.
An order was placed for 78 additional t-shirts after adult sizes sold out at the Senior Center.
T-shirts sell for $20 via cash, check, Venmo, or PayPal.
The committee is looking into an online print-on-demand vendor for collared shirts and other merchandise.
topics.outcome: New t-shirt inventory will be distributed to Town House and Senior Center sales locations, and the brick database will be finalized.

topics.title: School outreach, meeting workflow, and cultural grants
topics.summary: The committee discussed expanding student outreach beyond Algonquin Regional High School to Assabet Valley Vocational Technical High School, which has active photography, design, and art programs. Members agreed to submit subcommittee updates one week prior to meetings to keep sessions focused on actionable decisions. Deadlines for Massachusetts Cultural Council and Local Cultural Council grants were noted for the upcoming fall.
key_details: Members suggested partnering with Assabet Valley Voc Tech's art and photography programs.
Working group leaders were asked to send agenda updates to Vanessa one week before meetings.
Mass Cultural Council festival grants open on rolling deadlines in the fall with typical two-month submission windows.
topics.outcome: Members will reach out to Assabet Valley contacts and monitor upcoming grant application windows.
